title: 高阳台·送陈君衡被召
title_en: Gao Yang Tai: Seeing Off Chen Junheng, Summoned North
author: 周密

text_note.zh: 语料库作“风敧”，通行本作“风欹”，两字意思相同，都是歪斜。题目按通行本补上“送陈君衡被召”。
text_note.en: The corpus writes the word for tilted with a rare variant character; the common text uses the usual form. Both mean the same. The title follows the common text, which adds the occasion: seeing off Chen Junheng.

readings.zh: 朝天，去朝廷拜见皇帝，“朝”读 cháo。
readings.en: It means going to court to see the ruler, so the character is read cháo.
It means tilted to one side, read qī.
Here it means must be, or surely will, so it is read yīng.

readings.zh: 燕山，山名，“燕”读 yān，不读燕子的 yàn。
readings.en: Yan Mountains is a place name, so the character is read yān, not yàn as in swallow.
It means to come back, so it is read huán.

glosses.zh: 照野：照亮了原野。形容旗子又多又鲜艳。
glosses.en: zhào yě: lighting up the fields. The flags are so many and so bright.

glosses.zh: 旌旗：各种旗子。
glosses.en: jīng qí: flags and banners.

glosses.zh: 朝天：到京城去朝见皇帝。
glosses.en: cháo tiān: going to the capital to see the ruler.

glosses.zh: 平沙：平坦的沙地，指北方的大平原。
glosses.en: píng shā: flat sandy land, the wide plains of the north.

glosses.zh: 宝带金章：镶宝石的腰带，金子做的官印。这是做大官的打扮。
glosses.en: bǎo dài jīn zhāng: a jeweled belt and a gold seal of office. This is how a high official dresses.

glosses.zh: 尊前：酒杯前，指在酒席上。尊，同“樽”，酒杯。
glosses.en: zūn qián: in front of the wine cup, that is, at the feast.

glosses.zh: 茸帽：毛皮做的帽子，北方人冬天戴。
glosses.en: róng mào: a fur hat, worn in the cold north.

glosses.zh: 秦关汴水：秦地的关口，汴河的流水。这些都在北方，汴水边的汴京原来是北宋的都城。
glosses.en: qín guān biàn shuǐ: the mountain passes of the old Qin lands and the Bian River. They are all in the north. Bianjing, by the Bian River, was once the capital of the Northern Song.

glosses.zh: 经行地：路上会经过的地方。
glosses.en: jīng xíng dì: the places you will pass on the way.

glosses.zh: 登临：登高望远。
glosses.en: dēng lín: climbing high to look far.

glosses.zh: 都付新诗：都写进新的诗里。
glosses.en: dōu fù xīn shī: put it all into new poems.

glosses.zh: 纵英游：尽情地和英才们一起游玩。纵，放开、尽情。
glosses.en: zòng yīng yóu: enjoying outings freely with fine, gifted friends. Zòng means letting go, as much as you like.

glosses.zh: 叠鼓：一阵接一阵地打鼓。
glosses.en: dié gǔ: drums beaten again and again.

glosses.zh: 清笳：清亮的胡笳声。胡笳是北方的一种吹奏乐器。
glosses.en: qīng jiā: the clear sound of the hujia, a reed pipe played in the north.

glosses.zh: 名姬：有名的歌女。
glosses.en: míng jī: famous singing girls.

glosses.zh: 酒酣：酒喝得正痛快。
glosses.en: jiǔ hān: in the full joy of drinking.

glosses.zh: 燕山：山名，在今天北京一带。元朝的都城大都就在这里。
glosses.en: yān shān: the Yan Mountains, around today's Beijing. The Yuan capital Dadu was there.

glosses.zh: 晓陇：清晨的山冈。陇，山冈、高地。
glosses.en: xiǎo lǒng: hills at dawn. Lǒng means a ridge or high ground.

glosses.zh: 投老：到了老年。
glosses.en: tóu lǎo: having reached old age.

glosses.zh: 残年：剩下不多的岁月。
glosses.en: cán nián: the few years left.

glosses.zh: 方回：北宋词人贺铸，字方回，他写过江南愁思的名句。这里周密借他来说自己。
glosses.en: fāng huí: He Zhu, a Northern Song poet, whose courtesy name was Fanghui. He wrote famous lines about sorrow in the south. Here Zhou Mi uses him to mean himself.

glosses.zh: 绿：使……变绿。
glosses.en: lǜ: to turn something green.

glosses.zh: 南归：回到南方来。
glosses.en: nán guī: to come back south.

glosses.zh: 关情：牵动感情，最让人放不下。
glosses.en: guān qíng: touching the heart, the thing one cannot let go.

glosses.zh: 折尽梅花：古人有折梅花寄给远方朋友的故事。这里说梅花折完了，相思还是寄不出去。
glosses.en: zhé jìn méi huā: in an old story a man broke off a plum branch and sent it to a friend far away. Here all the plum blossoms are picked, yet the longing still cannot be sent.

translation.zh: 旗子多得照亮了原野，
translation.en: Banners light up the open fields,

translation.zh: 车马成队，去京城朝见皇帝。
translation.en: carriages and horses head for the court.

translation.zh: 万里平沙，天好像压得很低。
translation.en: Flat sand runs ten thousand li, and the sky hangs low.

translation.zh: 你系着宝带，挂着金印，
translation.en: You wear a jeweled belt and a gold seal,

translation.zh: 酒席前，毛皮帽子被风吹歪。
translation.en: and at the feast the wind tilts your fur hat.

translation.zh: 秦地的关口，汴河的流水，都是你要经过的地方，
translation.en: Passes of the old Qin lands, the Bian River: you will travel past them all.

translation.zh: 我想你登高远望的时候，
translation.en: When you climb high and look far,

translation.zh: 一定会把感慨都写进新诗。
translation.en: you will put it all into new poems.

translation.zh: 你会尽情地和英才们游玩，
translation.en: You will go out freely with gifted friends,

translation.zh: 听着一阵阵鼓声和清亮的胡笳，
translation.en: with drum after drum and the clear hujia pipe,

translation.zh: 身边是骏马和有名的歌女。
translation.en: fine horses and famous singers at your side.

translation.zh: 酒喝到痛快的时候，你该正对着燕山的大雪，
translation.en: When the wine runs high, you will be facing the snow of the Yan Mountains,

translation.zh: 那时河水结冰，月光也像冻住了，
translation.en: the rivers frozen, even the moonlight seeming frozen,

translation.zh: 清晨山冈上云在飞。
translation.en: and clouds flying over the hills at dawn.

translation.zh: 我已经老了，只剩下不多的岁月，
translation.en: I am old now, with few years left.

translation.zh: 留在江南，还有谁会想起我这个“贺方回”？
translation.en: Here in the south, who will think of me, an old poet like He Zhu?

translation.zh: 东风渐渐吹绿了西湖边的柳树，
translation.en: The east wind slowly turns the West Lake willows green.

translation.zh: 大雁已经飞回来了，
translation.en: The wild geese have already come back,

translation.zh: 你却还没有回到南方。
translation.en: but you have not yet come home to the south.

translation.zh: 最让我放不下的是：
translation.en: What touches my heart most:

translation.zh: 就算折光了梅花，
translation.en: even if I pick every plum blossom,

translation.zh: 也难把我的思念寄给你。
translation.en: I can hardly send my longing to you.

background.zh: 陈君衡就是陈允平，是周密的朋友，也是词人。南宋灭亡以后，元朝征召江南有名的读书人到北方的大都（今北京）去。陈允平也被召去，周密写了这首词给他送行。上半首想象朋友一路北上的热闹和风光，下半首写自己留在江南的孤单和思念。
background.en: Chen Junheng was Chen Yunping, Zhou Mi's friend and also a ci poet. After the Southern Song fell, the Yuan rulers summoned well-known scholars from the south to their capital Dadu, today's Beijing. Chen was summoned too, and Zhou Mi wrote this to see him off. The first half imagines the grand, busy journey north. The second half tells of Zhou Mi alone in the south, missing his friend.

author_note.zh: 周密，号草窗，南宋末年的词人，和吴文英并称“二窗”。他住在杭州一带，宋朝灭亡后不肯去元朝做官，写了很多回忆故国的书和词。这首词里的伤感，也和亡国之痛连在一起。
author_note.en: Zhou Mi, also called Caochuang, was a ci poet at the end of the Southern Song. With Wu Wenying he was known as the Two Windows. He lived around Hangzhou. After the Song fell he refused to serve the Yuan, and wrote many books and lyrics remembering the lost country. The sadness in this lyric is tied to that loss too.

appreciation.zh: 上半首写得很热闹：旗子照亮原野，车马成队，朋友穿着官服，在北风里喝酒、写诗、听鼓乐。可是“秦关汴水”是原来宋朝的土地，现在却成了别人的，热闹里藏着说不出的苦。下半首一下子冷下来：燕山的大雪、冰冻的河、清晨的云，是朋友要面对的北方；西湖的绿柳、回来的大雁，是周密留守的江南。雁回来了，人还没回来。最后折尽梅花也寄不出相思，把朋友情和故国情都写得又深又长。
appreciation.en: The first half is full of noise and color: banners light the fields, carriages roll on, and the friend in official dress drinks, writes poems and hears drums in the north wind. But the old Qin passes and the Bian River were once Song land, and now they belong to others. Under the noise lies a pain that cannot be spoken. The second half turns cold. Heavy snow on the Yan Mountains, frozen rivers and dawn clouds are the north the friend must face. Green willows at West Lake and returning geese are the south where Zhou Mi stays. The geese come back, but the friend does not. At the end, even every plum blossom picked cannot carry his longing. Friendship and grief for the lost country both run deep and long.
